newsitem.title: USA: Coastal files to export natgas to Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Coastal files to export natgas to Mexico.

text.p: Coastal Corp said Monday its Coastal States Gas Transmission Co subsidiary has filed with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission requesting authorization to construct and operate natural gas facilities at the United States-Mexican boundary.
The border crossing would be part of an international pipeline project connecting large natural gas reserves in South Texas to a growing natural gas market in Mexico.
Coastal said the project calls for construction of an 18 mile pipeline which will enable exports from the Bob West Field, now producing 200 million cubic feet daily.
Producers in the Bob West field include Coastal, Tesoro Petroleum Corp, KCS Energy Inc and TransTexas Gas Corp.
Coastal spokesman Steve Eames said the size and cost of the export project will be determined following completion of marketing studies, the timing of which is not yet announced.
The company said the project would allow interconnections with various intrastate pipelines in the area.
In Mexico, it continued, the border crossing would connect with a facility to be constructed by a Coastal States affiliate being formed in Mexico.
Coastal said the market for natural gas around Monterrey, Mexico, is projected to grow to 600 million cubic feet per day by the year 2000 fromn 400 million in 1995.
It said the border crossing would be located near the City of Roma, Texas, and Ciudad Miguel Aleman in the State of Tamaulipas.

The recent amendment to the Mexican Constitution and subsequent changes to regulations of the comision Reguladora de Energia, Mexico's energy regulatory commission, allow both state-owned and private concerns to obtain authorizations to build and operate natural gas transmission facilities on an open-acess, competitive basis, Coastal explained.
The company said Coastal States' Mexican affiliate will seek authorization from CRE for the proposed Mexican pipeline which would provide a connection with the existing Pemex pipeline system.
